_what: controls for the Writer x Reader factorial

cache_separation_across_writers._what: the response cache cannot serve a writer-gpt-oss answer to a writer-Gemma request. POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST: without a demonstrated HIT, a 'miss' proves only that the cache is dead.

aa_determinism_gpt_oss_120b._what: reader gpt-oss, writer Gemma: byte-identical WITHOUT-arm requests issued as SEPARATE calls (memory_repr is in the key). Identical content => deterministic at temperature 0 on the real shape.

aa_determinism_gemma_4_31B_it._what: reader Gemma, writer Gemma: byte-identical WITHOUT-arm requests issued as SEPARATE calls (memory_repr is in the key). Identical content => deterministic at temperature 0 on the real shape.

reader_gptoss._what: SESSION-MATCHED: writer gpt-oss vs writer Gemma, reader_gptoss, both executed 2026-10-01. The WITHOUT arm contains NO memory and F-GATE 4 proved its request bytes identical, so it MUST be identical here.
reader_gptoss._note: a difference here is a DEFECT, not a finding.

reader_gemma._what: SESSION-MATCHED: writer gpt-oss vs writer Gemma, reader_gemma, both executed 2026-10-01. The WITHOUT arm contains NO memory and F-GATE 4 proved its request bytes identical, so it MUST be identical here.
reader_gemma._note: a difference here is a DEFECT, not a finding.

cross_session_drift_that_forced_the_reru._what: CROSS-SESSION (published 2026-09-30 vs today): the SAME WITHOUT-arm request bytes, re-issued a day later.
cross_session_drift_that_forced_the_reru._note: This is NOT a writer comparison -- it is the endpoint's cross-session stability, and it is why every arm was re-run in one session. A non-zero count here is a finding about the ENDPOINT.

truncation_accounting._what: On Gemma a truncation returns a plausible FRAGMENT, not null content. Scored, it is a wrong answer that drives dU negative and MANUFACTURES a harmful memory. The guard tests three observables; the ARITHMETIC one (completion_tokens >= max_tokens) is counted separately because the server has been measured reporting neither reason field.
truncation_accounting.\ud83d\udd34_READ_THE_CACHE_COUNTS_CORRE: P1Client raises the truncation guard BEFORE it stores to the cache (client.py: _assert_not_truncated then cache.store), so a REFUSED truncation is never written to the cache at all. The cache counts below are therefore 'truncations ADMITTED', which is 0 BY CONSTRUCTION on a strict arm -- they are NOT evidence that no truncation occurred. The number that shows how often it DID occur is the row error-code count (truncated_nonempty_at_token_budget / empty_output_finish_length) below; the number that shows none was SCORED is rows_with_an_error_code_AND_a_non_null_delta. An absent check must never read as a passing one.

malformed_structured_validator_controls._what: Gemma produced ZERO malformed structured writes. A rate of 0 from a validator never shown to reject is not a measurement, so the validator is made to FIRE on four planted defects AND replayed against the gpt-oss outputs it already rejected.

writer_collapsed_distinct_segments._what: two DIFFERENT source segments compressed to byte-identical memory text. The ids are content hashes, so they collide and the validator reports duplicate_row_id. This is a property of the WRITER.
writer_collapsed_distinct_segments._finding: Gemma collapsed 1 summary text(s) across 2 segments; gpt-oss collapsed 0. Gemma writes ~2x shorter summaries, and at that compression two distinct episodes can land on the same words.
writer_collapsed_distinct_segments._does_it_affect_any_number: NO. The analysis joins on (memory_unit_locator, future_task_id), which is positional and cannot collide; the affected cells stay separate in the matched set. It WOULD have corrupted any analysis joining on memory_id -- which is exactly why this project's join rule forbids that.
